title: I built a folklore-collecting game from a real folktale database
author: thoughts-and-priors
selftext:
I’m a researcher who studies folktales computationally. Over the past few weeks I’ve been experimenting with games as a way to present research. This one, Sagenland, was built with Claude Code (Opus 5.5, high effort) and draws on the Folktale Database of the Low Countries (https://www.verhalenbank.nl): real Dutch legends about devils at crossroads, witte wieven on the heath, will-o’-the-wisps, and neighbours who bewitch your cows.

You’re a 19th/20th-century-style folktale collector with twelve days and a notebook, travelling between villages on an old regional map. On your travels you meet all kinds of people: A shepherd “has seen things”, an old man who knows everything is ill and may die before you reach him, a shy teller says nothing until you name a tale. Ask about witches too soon and the visit is over.

At the end, the game uses your notebook to estimate how many stories you missed, the way researchers estimate what an archive is missing. Then it shows you the real number. The estimate always falls short, because you didn’t collect at random. You went back to good tellers, followed tips, and asked about what interested you. That’s exactly the bias real collectors built into the archives we study today.

[https://www.karsdorp.io/sagenland](https://www.karsdorp.io/sagenland)

comments.author: No-Blacksmith7127
comments.body: Turning real folklore into a game where you collect stories is a pretty cool idea lol. Are you planning to add folklore from other regions too? Also, feel free to share it on r/OpenLobby sometime! It's a small indie gaming sub I run, and I'd love to see more of this project there.

replies.author: thoughts-and-priors
replies.body: Data of this quality and level of detail is quite rare, unfortunately, but there are some regions that could be added. We have a fair amount of stories from the area north of Amsterdam, for example. Thanks for the suggestion!
